summary: # Marvelous Designer Quick Start (2025 Update) - Part 4: Arrange Panels ## Setting the 2D Background First, click on the right button in the blank area of the 2D window to set the 2D background. Then click on **Reset** to reset the 2D background. ## Organizing 2D Panels Before starting the 3D arrangement, we can first organize the 2D panels in the 2D window, such as the parallel panels. 1. Select the two front panels in the frame. 2. Click on the right button on the panel to select **Align**. 3. Then select **Up** to align the two panels vertically. ## Rearranging Panels in 3D Next, go to the 3D toolbar and select **Rearrange 2D Arrangement**, then choose **All** to align the panels in the 3D window to match the arrangement of the 2D panel. ## Arranging Panels Around the Virtual Model We will now arrange the panels around the virtual model using the arrangement point. 1. Press **Ctrl + A** to select all the panels. 2. Click on the panel to reveal a positional ball. ### Understanding the Positional Ball In the default situation, the positional ball is targeted at the viewing angle of the screen. When rotating the viewing angle, the three different colors of the X, Y, and Z lines will not align and will always remain in the relative position of the lens view. To make it easier to use, we can click on the right button in the 3D background to select the positional ball. There are three options here: - **Screen Coordinates:** The default setting based on the screen view. - **Partial Coordinates:** The coordinates of the object itself. For instance, if I have a butterfly node from the outside, rotating this butterfly node will cause the positional ball to rotate with it. - **World Coordinates:** The positional ball will be fixed to the world coordinates. You can choose the appropriate coordinate system according to your needs. Here, I choose the **Partial Coordinates**. Note that the panels created in the software will use world coordinates, while models imported from external sources will use their original coordinates. ## Aligning Panels to the Virtual Model Select all the panels in the software and drag the green line to align the panels with the position of the virtual model. Alternatively, you can drag the yellow square to align the panels. ### Displaying the Virtual Model Layout Next, go to the virtual model display list in the 3D view menu. Select the display point and display layout. - The green circle around the virtual model indicates the layout. - The blue point on the layout board is the layout point. When selecting a panel, the mouse will stop at the layout point, allowing you to predict the layout effect. The center of the panel will be placed on this layout point and then rotate along the layout board. ### Arranging Sleeve Panels Click on the layout point to arrange the sleeve panels. You will notice that when the panels are arranged, the panels on the opposite side are also arranged. If there is a gray circle around the layout point, this indicates an alignment point. When the panels are arranged on the alignment point, the opposite side of the panel will automatically be arranged. ## Managing the Display Layout Board When you turn on the display layout board, you may accidentally select the layout board when clicking on the panel. To prevent non-operational issues, we can turn off the display layout board. ### Working with Multiple Panels When selecting multiple panels, you can place them as a whole in the layout. 1. Click on the layout board. 2. Press the **Shift** key and click on two front panels to place them on the corresponding layout point. You will see that the two panels are arranged together. The keys in the 3D window will also react simultaneously to the arrangement effect. ## Adjusting Panel Layouts We can also separate the front panels; however, after arranging, we may find that the panels overlap. To manage the layout, you can find the layout option in the property editor. By adjusting the position of the **X-Row** and **Y-Row**, the panels will be separated from each other and adjusted to a position slightly higher than the border line. The arrangement option is also set to be symmetrical. Since we want to sew the border line afterward, we must ensure that when the panel is arranged, the following sewing lines will not cause the panel to intersect with the body during sewing. ## Placing the Back Panel Next, place the back panel in the appropriate position. By adjusting the position of the panel, you can separate it from the model or bring it closer to the model. This adjustment will ensure that the panel does not intersect with the model. Adjust the **Y-Row** to make the panel line exceed the model. Then, place the pocket in the location of the chest. ### Avoiding Misoperations When selecting a panel, if the mouse stops at the point of arrangement, it may accidentally rearrange the panel, causing misoperations. To avoid this, when we do not need the point of arrangement, the axis of the positional ball can be pulled out of the pocket of the board to avoid cross-stitching. ## Final Adjustments and Saving The 3D arrangement of the board is based on the direction of the 2D window. You can go to the arrangement and direction in the attribute editor to adjust the angle and return the board to the correct arrangement position. If the board overlaps with other boards and cannot be selected, you can select a board that is blocked and press **Shift + Q** to hide it. Then, drag the axis of the positional ball to the appropriate position of the pocket board. Finally, you can save the project file and prepare to learn the following sewing techniques.
